Hi Amelia — quick technical summary below (putting the detailed caveats at the bottom). I'm attaching the retention matrix and a small replication diagram.

Short answer (practical):
- Live store: deletion via the API marks data as erased immediately in the primary region; the object is removed from the primary object store within seconds to minutes depending on in-flight requests.
- Snapshots (point-in-time): snapshots are immutable by design. A deletion in the live store does NOT retroactively remove data from existing snapshots. Instead snapshots are subject to the snapshot retention policy: by default EU snapshots are retained for 90 days and are pruned at the next retention sweep.
- DR replicas (async cross-region replication): replication is asynchronous. New writes (and deletes represented as tombstones) are propagated to replicas within the normal replication lag (usually under 15 minutes, sometimes up to 2 hours under heavy load). However, final physical removal in the replica's storage tier depends on the replica's local retention sweep and GC schedule (typically aligned with snapshot retention windows).

Expedited erasure workflow (what we can do today):
1) Customer raises an expedited-delete ticket via Support with the data identifiers + legal basis.
2) Our Security team validates the request and coordinates an expedited sweep: we mark all matching snapshots for expedited prune and escalate GC jobs across replicas.
3) If data is held in cold offsite archives or tape-equivalent storage, we provide an estimated erase window but cannot guarantee sub-24h removal for those mediums.

Expected timelines we provide to customers (non-binding operational guidance):
- Live store: seconds -> minutes (immediate logical deletion)
- Standard snapshots: removal aligned to next retention sweep (0–90 days depending on policy and snapshot age)
- Expedited sweep (after validated support ticket): target 72 hours to remove data from snapshot and replica indexes; physical reclaim may take longer for deep-cold tiers.

Caveats and exceptions:
- Legal holds / litigation: data under legal hold is excluded from any deletion action until released by the customer or proper legal order.
- Immutable backups held for audit or regulatory reasons may be outside the expediteable window — these are listed in the retention matrix.
- If a replica resides in a jurisdiction with tighter data erasure rules, local operators may require additional attestations.

I'll attach the retention matrix (redwood-retention-matrix-v2.xlsx) and a short diagram (snapshot-replication-diagram.png) for your DPO. We can also provide a SOC2 summary if you need evidence of process.

Amelia — adding the compliance perspective and the exact steps we will take when ClearMed requests an expedited delete.

1) Intake: Support ticket > Compliance triage. We require a minimal set of information: user identifiers, time range, API keys & account id, and the legal basis. PII in the ticket is handled in a secure intake form (link below).
2) Scope & proof: We run a scoped search across live stores, snapshot indices, and replication logs to enumerate all copies and snapshots containing the identifiers. We provide a short report to the customer listing the locations and estimated removal windows.
3) Action: Upon validation we trigger an expedited prune job across the affected snapshot IDs. For async replicas, we send tombstone propagation signals and prioritize GC tasks on affected nodes.

Timelines we record internally (SLA targets we aim for):
- Acknowledgement: within 4 business hours of ticket receipt (business hours: 09:00–18:00 local for primary account region).
- Scope report: within 24 business hours.
- Expedited prune attempt: targeted within 72 hours from validation.
- Full physical reclaim: depends on storage class; cold archives can take 7–30 days.

Note on jurisdictional constraints: we do not migrate or force-destruct replicas located in a third-party managed cloud tenancy without coordination. If a customer's EU data was replicated to a partner-managed archive with separate legal controls, we will coordinate but cannot unilaterally destroy third-party-managed media — we provide attestation and escalation support.

If ClearMed wants a firmer contractual guarantee for expedited deletion across all tiers, we can describe a Dedicated offering addendum that narrows retention windows and adds on-site erase procedures. Happy to outline that if you want.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
